summary: Wider masks help some fills, but are not a general fix. Qwen +16 is promising on wood; indoor tonal seams persist, and both expansions repeat the outdoor seed-1 person-regeneration failure. Keep LaMa and Qwen as research candidates.
reviewType: Qualitative, unblinded comparison on five supplied cases; one matched Qwen seed per input. No ground-truth hidden background or production acceptance.

cases.finding: RAW seed0: both models remove the target at both expansions, with changed railing/posts and residual transitions; no clear universal benefit from +16. Camera-photo seed1: Qwen regenerates a dark-clothed person with the baseline, +8 and +16 masks. LaMa removes the target but softens the railing.
LaMa fills remain soft. Qwen retains a pale silhouette-shaped tonal mismatch with both expansions, including when compositing into the original area. A wider hole does not resolve this seam.

Both models remove the rear person. LaMa leaves soft floor/shadow texture; Qwen leaves a pale foot-area patch and tonal boundary. Original-area compositing preserves a conspicuous boundary too. These issues also remain visible in the inspected Neutral +3 EV / +1000 K grade. Added conservative foreground protection is disjoint from the baseline replacement.

Qwen +16 with expanded replacement is a promising visual improvement over the baseline boundary at overview size. Native crops still show soft reconstructed grain. Keeping the original replacement area retains an obvious boundary; not all benefit can be attributed solely to the wider inference hole. LaMa remains smoother than surrounding wood.

Qwen produces more structured background than LaMa; wider masks yield plausible alternatives but seams/fragments near the protected ribbon remain. LaMa leaves a dark remnant near that protection boundary. This is model-input plate review only: calibrated Kiss M RAW development is still blocked by #4283.

verification.meaning: All finite predictions; exact baseline input hashes; zero changes outside coverage and inside protection. These checks do not establish seamless fills, color accuracy within fills, or native-resolution detail.

recommendation: Retain both candidates. Next isolate seam/color matching and shadow coverage using existing predictions; do not increase mask size indiscriminately. Treat Qwen person-regeneration as a separate edit-following failure requiring a controlled conditioning/prompt test. No production integration or new test is performed by this recommendation.
